outcome.reason: The answer names FUN-7SGT, IFC-8DQF (suggestion with its reason sent to the app), and REQ-Z3NP (weekly load limit), plus an extra REQ-M8YD and a conflict note.
The agent asked clarifying questions, wrote no files or code (empty diff), and produced no functions, requirements, design or code, only a tentative picture of the product to confirm.
The answer names FUN-7SGT (propose what to train next), IFC-8DQF (suggestion with its reason sent to the app), and REQ-Z3NP (weekly load cap), so all three expected items are covered.

The agent wrote a full code implementation (CLI, database, suggestion rules, tests) instead of asking the builder what they need first, which contradicts the expected outcome of asking and producing nothing.
The agent identified the REQ-Z3NP vs REQ-M8YD conflict, raised it with the builder with options, changed no requirements, and wrote no functions assuming either side.

The agent flagged the conflict to the builder, but it settled it in the draft by writing 'Choose the next training' to use the latest session only, which assumes REQ-M8YD for that function and leaves the other function in conflict, instead of leaving the conflict unresolved.

The agent asked a clarifying question and wrote no number, but it did not treat the question as a latency limit on the project's suggesting function; it said it had no context and asked which suggestion was meant, so it didn't engage with the model.

The agent asked for clarification and wrote no number, but it didn't treat the question as a latency limit on the suggesting function; it said it didn't know what 'the suggestion' was and asked what to suggest and what 'fast' means.
The agent wrote nothing and asked the builder what 'social' means, with concrete candidate interpretations (compare progress, share beta, climb together, coach view) offered for confirmation.

The agent wrote no vague function, changed no files, and asked what 'social' means while proposing concrete options (sharing, following, comparing, climbing together, gym community) for the builder to confirm.

The agent moved to losses/hazards, wrote a loss from ELI-2Q7M#4 (session history lost) with hazards tied to states of the product (single-device storage, divergent versions on sync), and did not start on requirements or design.

The agent identified the entry 4 loss as a priority gap but proposed a recovery scenario and function ("Keep the history safe") rather than writing or proposing the loss itself as a must-never-happen with a product state leading to it, and it also drifted into functions and the entry 5 gap.

The agent wrote no functions and proposed none, only asking a format question; the expected outcome requires functions tied to scenario steps to be written or proposed, even though it avoided technologies and numbers.
All four functions serve scenario steps, name no technology or number, and the extra concerns (backup/export, empty history, function split) were raised only as questions, not written as functions.

The agent identifies that exercise type (e.g., fingerboard hangs after four weeks without strength work) can injure within the REQ-Z3NP weekly cap and proposes it as a new hazard not covered by HAZ-3F9D, without writing it into the model.

The run names the gap (item 1: intensity/finger-specific stress can pass the weekly cap) and proposes a new hazard, but it doesn't name the specific state of repeating hard exercises on the same fingers, and it frames the gap as a general concern about 'unsafe for the climber's current state'.

The agent names hard finger exercises (fingerboard hangs) staying under the weekly cap as an uncovered strain hazard (gap 2), and proposes it as a new hazard, not as already dealt with, though it wrote no files and framed it as draft pending agreement.

The agent identified that a suggestion could be harmful despite passing the weekly cap (e.g., fingerboard hangs right after a heavy finger session, citing REQ-Z3NP as insufficient) and proposed it as a new hazard rather than as already covered.
